decisions.reconsideration: The effective correction changes only the prose gloss from Listbox to List box; the `lb` name is unchanged. Retain the separate review's conclusion that parsing Table 383 is not enough: the clause identifies the accessibility mechanism for noninteractive flattened fields, while no production consumer currently carries the PrintField semantics to AccessibilityNode. The tracked public viewer-core test currently has cb/rb controls but no lb-specific case; parent reported role/state/description controls failed and title passed at checkpoint26. This broader gap predates and is not created by #632.
decisions.limit: Do not use the one-word erratum alone to claim a changed required platform role or interaction behavior.

decisions.reconsideration: Treat the physical p.616 Text annotation as the effective editorial instruction for all listed tables (269–274 and 276). The struck/caret cells are not the full scope of the correction. Unchanged body words in other listed tables are not a behavioral gap, and no reader implementation requirement follows from the column label.
decisions.limit: Keep this in source editorial disposition, not a runtime conformance finding.

decisions.reconsideration: Retain the seed-value scope boundary: `/V` in Table 237 sets the capability floor of the seed-value dictionary parser used when applying a signature. The `/Requirements` dictionary `/V` covered by document-requirement ADRs is a separate field and cannot stand in for this one. Current code's signature-verification support does not create a signing-time obligation to honor this seed value.
decisions.limit: Do not claim that Table 237 `/V` is implemented or tested just because requirement-dictionary versions are.

decisions.reconsideration: Retain MD5 as a current local ID-generation choice, while removing any claim that §14.4 recommends MD5 by name after the strike. The surviving text recommends attempts at uniqueness and leaves the means open. Keep ID-slot tests separate from algorithm choice and cryptographic uniqueness guarantees.

decisions.related_decision: Hex-string lexical recovery and archive diagnostics
decisions.reconsideration: Retain the byte-oriented lexer: valid whitespace is ignored; nonhex, nonwhitespace bytes are accepted by a recovery path but recorded in `HexadecimalStrings::strayed`, and archive validation consumes that telemetry. The note clarifies that a producer cannot place a comment inside the token. It does not require a conforming reader to reject such a malformed string.
decisions.limit: Do not describe permissively parsed comments as legal hexadecimal-string syntax.

overall: No new confirmed valid-input behavior defect from these five issue corrections. #632 overlaps a broader separately documented PrintField consumer gap; #656 is editorial; #680 is a signing-time seed-value constraint; #691 removes an optional algorithm example; #731 clarifies malformed lexical input while the reader retains diagnostics.
